note: Shows choosing melodies by filter: each melody-singer names a difficulty and a stage with pick instead of a tune number, the second a step harder than the first. The why says what makes a step tune easier than a skip, the step tune comes back in A by the Key selector, and the text says what Play starts (the tune and the mic) and what to sing on.

exercise.title: Two tunes: steps, then skips
exercise.why: In a tune that moves by step each note sits right next to the last one, while a skip asks you to hear the next note before you jump to it, so the step tune comes first.

cells.text:
A tune on Do, Re and Mi. Press Play below to hear it: the mic starts with it, and your pitch shows on the staff. Sing along on the note names.
Once it feels easy, try it in another key. Use the Key selector below to change the key, then press Play to hear the tune there.
When you change the key, the notes change but the tune keeps its shape.
A longer tune in D that skips between Do, Mi and Sol, then steps back down. Look at the staff first and guess how it goes. Press Play below to check your guess, then sing along on "la".
